Description: A neoplasm with acinar cell differentiation, arising from the secretory cells of exocrine glands such as the pancreas, salivary glands, or lungs.
A neoplasm arising from or exhibiting the features of glandular epithelium; encompasses a broad morphological category including adenomas, adenocarcinomas, and related glandular tumors.
A neoplasm arising from skin appendage structures, including hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and eccrine or apocrine sweat glands.
A neoplasm derived from epithelial cells, the cells lining the surfaces and cavities of the body.
A benign, borderline, or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of an epithelial and a fibrous component. Representative examples are fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumor.
A poorly circumscribed neoplasm arising from the soft tissues, characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and an infiltrative growth pattern.
A neoplasm arising from germ cells, the primordial cells that give rise to eggs and sperm.
A neoplasm characterized by the presence of multinucleated giant cells intermixed with mononuclear stromal cells.
A neoplasm arising from glial cells of the central nervous system, including astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells.

Attribute: Granular Cell Tumors and Alveolar Soft Part Sarcomas

Description: A malignant clonal hematologic disorder involving hematopoietic stem cells, characterized by the presence of primitive or atypical myeloid or lymphoid cells in the bone marrow and blood.
A neoplasm arising from adipose (fat) tissue, ranging from benign lipomas to malignant liposarcomas.
A usually benign neoplasm arising from the meninges, the membranes that cover and protect the brain and spinal cord.
A neoplasm arising from mesothelial cells, which line the body cavities including the pleura, peritoneum, and pericardium.
A heterogeneous group of clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders characterized by ineffective blood cell production, peripheral blood cytopenias, and risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia.
A neoplasm arising from or exhibiting differentiation toward muscle tissue, encompassing tumors of smooth, skeletal, or cardiac muscle.
An abnormal tissue growth resulting from uncontrolled and progressive cell proliferation; may be benign or malignant.

A benign or malignant neoplasm arising from the perineural cells in the sheaths surrounding the nerves. Representative examples include neurofibroma, schwannoma, and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
A neoplasm arising from melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells found primarily in the skin and eye; includes both benign lesions (nevi) and malignant melanomas.

A neoplasm arising from tissues involved in tooth formation, including enamel organ, dental papilla, and dental follicle, most commonly arising in the jaw.
A neoplasm arising from paraganglia, specialized clusters of neuroendocrine cells that are part of the autonomic nervous system, located at various sites outside the adrenal medulla.
A neoplasm characterized by the clonal proliferation of plasma cells, the antibody-secreting terminally differentiated B-cells.

Attribute: Soft Tissue Tumors and Sarcomas; NOS
Description: A neoplasm arising from the non-epithelial, non-osseous supporting tissues of the body, including fat, fibrous tissue, muscle, peripheral nerves, and blood and lymph vessels.
A neoplasm arising from or exhibiting the features of squamous epithelium, ranging from benign squamous papillomas to squamous cell carcinomas.
A neoplasm arising from the synovial tissue lining joint cavities, tendon sheaths, and bursae.
A neoplasm arising from the epithelial cells of the thymus gland, spanning a spectrum from thymoma to thymic carcinoma.

A group of pregnancy-related proliferative disorders including non-neoplastic conditions and trophoblastic neoplasms such as invasive hydatidiform mole, gestational choriocarcinoma, and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor.
